learning.learning_goal: Understand percent as a rate per one hundred relative to a named whole.
learning.big_idea: Percent expresses a part-to-whole relationship on a common scale where the whole is 100 percent.
assumed_prior_knowledge: interpret equal parts of a fraction
novice_success_criteria: connect percent to a fraction and split the whole into equal shares

screens.label: Lesson 007 · Prototype
screens.title: What does a percent actually say?
screens.body: Percent means per hundred: it compares a part with a named whole on a scale of 100.
screens.callout: No conversion shortcut is assumed. We will build percent from the whole and equal parts.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: Is 40% simply the whole number 40?
screens.prompt: A battery is at 40%. What does the 40 describe?

choices.text: The battery contains the number 40 with no whole attached
40 of 100 equal parts of the full charge
choices.feedback: The full battery is the whole, represented as 100%; 40% describes 40 of those hundred equal parts.

choices.text: The battery always has 40 units of energy

hints: Read percent as “per hundred,” not as a detached number.

screens.label: Observe
screens.title: Represent one whole as 100 equal parts.

visual.ariaLabel: A one-hundred-cell grid with forty cells filled
visual.message: The entire grid is one whole, or 100%. Forty cells represent 40%.

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: Which forms describe the same amount?

visual.ariaLabel: Forty of one hundred equal cells filled
visual.message: 40 percent and 40/100 name the same part of this whole.

choices.text: 40% = 40 wholes
40% has the same amount in every situation, even when the whole changes

choices.feedback: The words “40 percent” and the fraction 40/100 both name 40 equal parts out of 100 parts of the same whole.

hints: The word percent supplies the denominator 100.
The percent sign tells you that the comparison uses 100.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: Name the whole before using the rate.

visual.ariaLabel: Twenty-five of one hundred equal cells filled
visual.message: 25% means 25 per 100 of the named whole.

screens.phraseMeaning: The same part of the same whole

definitions.meaning: a comparison measured per one hundred
a comparison that says how much for a set amount
different names for the same amount or relationship

screens.guidance: Before calculating, finish the sentence: 100% of what? Then ask how many equal percent shares fill that whole.

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: Name the whole; then read per hundred.
screens.hook: Percent = how many per 100 of a named whole.
screens.body: Use the part-to-whole relationship to rebuild the value instead of relying on an unexplained rule.
rebuildSteps: Interpret the percent as that many parts per 100.
Write the same relationship as a fraction with 100 equal parts.
Check whether the result is reasonable relative to the whole.
screens.boundary: The percent alone does not reveal an amount. Forty percent of $80 differs from forty percent of $200 because the base whole changed.

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: Which statement explains 25% of $80?

visual.ariaLabel: Twenty-five out of one hundred cells filled
visual.message: Four equal groups of 25% fill 100%, so 25% is one of four equal shares of the whole.

choices.text: $80 split into 4 equal shares gives $20 per share
choices.feedback: Four 25% shares rebuild 100%. Splitting the $80 whole into four equal shares gives $20 in each share.

choices.text: The answer is $25 because the percent says 25
The answer cannot be found because $80 is not the number 100

hints: Count how many 25% shares fill 100%, then split $80 into that many equal shares.

visual.ariaLabel: One quarter of a hundred grid filled
visual.message: Twenty-five per hundred is one of four equal shares because four groups of 25 fill 100.

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: Find 10% of $70 by meaning.

visual.ariaLabel: Ten out of one hundred equal cells filled
visual.message: Ten equal groups of 10% fill 100%, so 10% is one of ten equal shares.

choices.text: $10, because the percent says 10
$7, because ten equal shares rebuild $70
choices.feedback: Ten 10% shares rebuild 100%. Splitting the $70 whole into ten equal shares gives $7 in each share.

hints: Name $70 as the whole represented by 100%.
Count ten equal 10% shares in the whole, then divide $70 among those ten shares.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Reason without the grid.
screens.prompt: A $60 jacket is discounted by 20%. How much is the discount?

choices.text: $20, because the sign follows 20
$48, because that is the price after the discount
$12, because five equal shares rebuild the $60 whole
choices.feedback: Five groups of 20% rebuild 100%. Splitting the original $60 into five equal shares gives a $12 discount.

hints: The question asks for the discount, not the final price.
Use the original $60 as 100%. Five groups of 20% fill that whole.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: Reconstruct percent without a conversion rule.
screens.prompt: What two ideas must be identified before interpreting 37%?

choices.text: The named whole and 37 parts per 100 of that whole
choices.feedback: Percent is a rate only after the base whole is known.

choices.text: Only the whole number 37
A fixed amount of 37 no matter what the whole is

hints: Read the symbol as the words “per hundred.”

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Explain percent change in a new setting.
screens.prompt: A price falls from $80 to $60. Why is the decrease 25% of the original price?

choices.text: The decrease is 20% because the dollar change is 20
$20 is one of four equal shares of $80
choices.feedback: The original $80 is the whole. Four equal $20 shares rebuild it, so one $20 share is 25% of the original.

choices.text: The decrease is 25% because $60 is the whole

hints: Use the original $80 as 100% and ask how many $20 shares rebuild it.

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: Which explanation shows understanding?
screens.prompt: Choose the statement that explains percent.

choices.text: Percent is a detached whole number followed by a symbol.
Percent always tells an amount even when the whole is unknown.
Percent compares a part with a named whole on a per-hundred scale.

hints: Think about why the whole changed the dollar amount.

screens.title: You rebuilt percent from its meaning.
screens.body: You connected the whole, a per-hundred rate, equivalent forms, and a real amount.
screens.nextRecommendation: Prototype cluster complete. Adult-facing review is required before production approval.
